rationale: SAML assertion validation flaw: forged assertions authenticate; this is signature/login-flow validation, not an authorization decision.
After an admin demoted a user to guest, the user's existing session kept old roles, so the guest could still rename groups until re-login.
A token of tenant X could upsert labels of or unsubscribe a worker of tenant Y by UUID; worker was not checked against caller tenant. gRPC ops not in REST contract.
A user with copy permission could copy a file denied by filter patterns to an allowed name and read it; only destination was checked. Copy op not in provided contract.
A workflow submitter could set hostNetwork, serviceAccountName and securityContext in the Workflow spec despite strict template referencing; these were merged into pods.
Team admin without Add Members permission received team invite_id in /users/me/teams responses; sanitize wrongly kept it for managers.
Excess Kubernetes RBAC of a CSI service account on a compromised node; not an HTTP operation of the service.
Caller could read logs of another user's run (or any pod in namespace) via the run log endpoint; no authorization check against the run. Endpoint not in contract.
Namespaced HTTPRoute mirror bypasses ReferenceGrant via Kubernetes resources in the operator; not an HTTP operation of a REST service.
Any authenticated user, including Observer, could call debug/pprof endpoints reserved for admins; middleware now requires global admin role.
Any authenticated user could read and write file-column content of any row, including admin-only tables, via generic /yjs/:documentName websocket without row permission check.
Client-certificate CN matched to RBAC username allowed impersonation via gateway; authentication/credential validation flaw rather than an authorization rule.
Update validation mutated objects so validating admission webhooks saw old values; whether it is an access-control decision of the API is unclear.
Library component header names bypassed Camel inbound header filter in user-defined routes; no fixed HTTP operation of a service.
Misaligned security matchers let non-admin users call POST /import and /export, which require admin scope per contract.
Any authenticated low-privilege user could read the global API token signing key via the attributes endpoint; authorization check was missing.
